newsitem.title: UK: BG shares down on TransCo price review.
newsitem.headline: BG shares down on TransCo price review.

text.p: Shares in BG Plc, formerly known as British Gas, were indicated lower on Wednesday after the Monopolies and Mergers Commission recommended a one-off 21 percent cut in TransCo's charges to gas suppliers.
The shares were down 2-1/2p to 210p by 0706 GMT.

Industry regulator, Ofgas, said the reduced charges to gas suppliers would result in a 29 stg saving on the average domestic gas bill in the coming year, which is tougher than most analysts had expected.
"Everybody was talking about an initial price cut of 20 pounds and it turned out to be 29, so the headline figure is worse than anticipated," said Irene Himona, industry analyst at SocGen.

BG said the effect of the MMC's proposals would be to reduce TransCo's revenue by 5 percent in 1997/8 and 7 percent in 1998/9 followed by increases of 1-2 percent in each of the subsequent three years.
The company said it intended to write-down the value of TransCo's assets by around 5 billion stg and would revise its dividend policy in light of accounting changes.

"Overall the MMC's decision will result in a significant reduction in TransCo's cash flows over the next five years in line with the Ofgas proposals," Himona said. "Up until today we thought the dividend might be cut from 14.5p to 6p but it may now be a little more than that," she added.
The somewhat muted response from BG's share price reflected relief that the price review had finally been concluded, after a year of uncertainty, analysts said.
"It was worse than expected," said another analyst at a leading brokerage, "But I don't expect the shares to come off a lot."
Himona agreed that "At least we now know what is going to happen over the next five years and they have all agreed upon it."
